articles.title: West Ham confirm Scott Parker as head coach after sacking Nuno Espírito Santo
articles.summary: Parker takes over team eighth in Championship. He has overseen three promotions to Premier League. Scott Parker has been confirmed as West Ham’s head coach, taking over from Nuno Espírito Santo, who was sacked on Tuesday.
body: West Ham hope that Parker, a promotion specialist, can spark a revival after defeats in their past two matches. The 46-year-old has led Burnley, Bournemouth and Fulham into the top flight.

West Ham kept faith with Nuno after last season’s relegation from the Premier League but acted after they were beaten at home by West Brom last Saturday. Parker has been out of work since leaving Burnley after their relegation from the Premier League last April.

articles.summary: Deal would be worth more than £2bn. Cadillac are jointly owned by Mark Walter. Liverpool’s owner, Fenway Sports Group, has held talks about buying a majority stake in the Cadillac Formula One team for more than £2bn as Mark Walter continues to sell off his sporting assets amid allegations of…
body: Cadillac entered F1 this year as a joint venture between General Motors and Walter’s TWG Global, which sold its controlling interest in the NBA’s Los Angeles Lakers and a 13% stake in Chelsea this summer, and is also looking to sell Los Angeles Sparks, the WNBA team.

Walter is under investigation by the US Department of Justice and the Securities and Exchange Commission over alleged fraud involving the management of funds at his insurance companies Delaware Life, Clear Spring, and EquiTrust. TWG has said “there has been no fraud”.

articles.title: Sydney Swans player Tom Papley allegedly returns positive roadside drug test
articles.summary: Club says AFL forward returned ‘positive preliminary test indication’ NSW police issue a notice for driving with a suspended licence. The Sydney Swans forward Tom Papley has allegedly returned a positive preliminary drug test after being pulled over by New South Wales police on Monday.
body: The 30-year-old was stopped by police for a roadside licence check which led to a court attendance notice for driving with a suspended licence as well as a random drug test.
“Papley was issued with a court attendance notice for driving with a suspended licence due to non-payment of a parking fine,” the club said in a statement.

“During the roadside stop, Papley completed a random drug test which returned a positive preliminary test indication. A second sample was taken for analysis. The results from the second test are expected to take at least four weeks.”
Papley immediately advised the Swans of the matter and the club informed the AFL.

articles.title: Has a footballer ever run a marathon faster than James Milner? | The Knowledge
articles.summary: Plus: managers sacked after signing new deals, war victims commemorated on kits and the first club website (part II) Mail us with all of your questions and answers. It came as no surprise to the Knowledge that James Milner had spent the early months of his retirement training for – and then running…
body: In 2012 we ran a column listing footballers’ fastest marathon times, with the former Leicester playmaker Muzzy Izzet leading the pack on 3hr 22min 36sec at the 2011 London Marathon. That very respectable time has now been surpassed by the Premier League’s record appearance maker, so we thought we had better take a gulp of our isotonic energy drink and run through a few more tales of football’s marathon men and women.

More recent marathon attempts by either active or former footballers puts Izzet down in 12th place, just behind André Schürrle, who clocked 3hr 21min 25sec in Berlin last year, though clearly wanted a greater challenge than a mere 26.2 miles. This year, the 35-year-old completed the 167.7-mile six-stage Marathon des Sables in 51hr 41min 16sec, placing 675th overall. He also climbed Mont Blanc. But back to marathons, where the fastest time we can find for a female footballer is 3hr 40min 30sec by the former USA midfielder Lauren Holiday. She is closely followed by her good friends from the USWNT, Leslie Osborne (3hr 41min 33sec) and Abby Wambach (3hr 44min 25sec).

articles.title: Wilson returns as Wales call up uncapped Duncan
articles.summary: Harry Wilson is back in Wales' squad for their Nations League matches against Norway and Portugal, while goalkeeper Joe Duncan earns his first call.
body: Wilson has been one of Wales' most influential players in recent years but injuries mean the Leeds United attacking midfielder has not featured for his country since March.
His Leeds team-mate, centre-back Joe Rodon, also returns despite not playing since injuring his hamstring in August.
Cardiff City playmaker Rubin Colwill is recalled but fellow midfielder Jordan James is out after sustaining an injury while playing for Wolves against the Bluebirds last Saturday.
The only new call-up is 20-year-old keeper Duncan, who is on loan at National League side Southend United from Championship outfit Bristol City.

articles.title: From Derby to Champions League - Brown's journey to face Reds
articles.summary: Fenerbahce's Archie Brown on his unorthodox journey to Istanbul, the moment of madness against Galatasaray and what Liverpool can expect in Turkey on Wednesday evening.
body: For Archie Brown, playing for Fenerbahce against Liverpool in the Champions League on Wednesday will mark another step in the justification of his own "unorthodox" journey that began as a young boy in the Midlands.
Brown, 24, was born in Birmingham and started his youth career at West Brom before joining Derby, where he helped them to their only youth top-flight title.
He scored a hat-trick in a 5-2 win over an Arsenal U18s side that included Bukayo Saka 5-2 in the final between the North and South division winners.
Yet come 2021, the Englishman was frustrated by a lack of first-team opportunities and left to join Lausanne Sport in Switzerland at the age of 19.

articles.title: Fernandes hits back at 'lies' and claims players don't need to save Carrick's job
articles.summary: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has come out in support of head coach Michael Carrick, but reiterated that the players didn't need to save his job in their 3-2 comeback win against Roma.
body: United and Carrick looked dead and buried within the first 18 minutes as the Italian side took a two-goal lead in the early exchanges.

It prompted boos and protests from supporters, who threw tennis balls onto the pitch, but the Red Devils turned things around as a Fernandes penalty and a late Matheus Cunha double gave them their first win in 54 days.
The spirit shown in the performance suggested at least some on-pitch support for Carrick, whose tenure appeared to have been hanging on by a thread ever since the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth.

Fernandes was named on the bench for that game after publicly questioning the tactics in a sobering 4-1 defeat to Como four days prior. His words after Roma, though, were a lot more defiant than accusatory.

articles.summary: It was the most anticipated game of the group stages, and it was clear to see why as Tonga and Samoa did battle and both booked their spots in the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals.
body: Tonga beat Samoa 20-18 in the final group match in an electrifying battle between the two nations that have grown into rugby league forces over the last decade.
The fixture was truly a sight to behold with fans out in force and the atmosphere dialled up to a level we have never quite seen.

A change in eligibility rules enabled a contingent of Australian and New Zealand-born stars to pledge their allegiance to Tonga and Samoa as they decided to represent their family lineage, the State of Origin eligibility being expanded only helping to grow their cause.
It has meant that, for the big three of Australia, New Zealand, and England, two disrupters have arrived. And disrupt they have.

Brent Venables fired Ben Arbuckle and named Witten as Oklahoma’s interim offensive coordinator on Monday.

articles.title: Wilson, Rodon recalled to Wales squad for Nations League clashes
articles.summary: Wales boss Craig Bellamy has recalled several players, including Harry Wilson and Joe Rodon, for November's Nations League fixtures.
body: The Dragons sit third in Group A4 after beating Norway during the previous international break, but also suffering two defeats to Denmark and one against Portugal.
On Saturday November 14, they face Norway in Oslo, before a sold-out clash with Portugal at the Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday November 17.

Leeds winger Wilson withdrew from the squad for the previous camp in September with a quadricep injury, while club team-mate Rodon has seemingly recovered from a hamstring injury suffered during the 1-1 draw with Brentford on August 30.
Elsewhere, Man Utd goalkeeper Karl Darlow also returns to the squad, while U21 stopper Joe Duncan earns his first senior call-up.
